summary: The bill requires manufacturers of certain Medicare Part B drugs subject to maximum fair price negotiation to pay quarterly rebates equal to the gap between the standard ASP+6 payment and the lower MFP+6 amount (adjusted for coinsurance), while keeping provider payments at the higher rate and basing beneficiary coinsurance on the negotiated price.

scores.thoughts: The bill adjusts Medicare Part B reimbursement mechanics for selected drugs under maximum fair price negotiation by requiring manufacturer rebates deposited into the Supplementary Medical Insurance Trust Fund. This maintains provider payments at ASP+6 levels while recouping differences via rebates, resulting in no net expansion or reduction of government spending. The mechanism is fiscally neutral overall.
The bill contains no provisions related to taxes, tax rates, or tax policy. It solely addresses Medicare drug payment and rebate structures.

The bill directly amends Medicare Part B rules for drugs subject to IRA price negotiation. It preserves the market-based ASP+6 reimbursement formula for providers (via manufacturer rebates) and ties beneficiary coinsurance to the lower MFP+6 amount. This supports continuation of existing market-oriented reimbursement practices within the public Medicare program rather than shifting toward greater public rate-setting or universal coverage models.
